human_tolerance.notes: Judgement from the Wikipedia habitat text (woodland, shade and water preference); no urban-tolerance source was checked.

external.note: iNaturalist 42278 (P3151) and NCBI 9897 (P685) via Wikidata; the iNaturalist id was also returned by the public taxa search.

range.note: Wikipedia: 'from central and southern Kenya and northeastern Uganda ... to northern KwaZulu-Natal ... westward up to Namibia and southern Angola'. GBIF occurrence search, taxonKey 2441144, occurrenceStatus PRESENT, country facets (checked 2026-11-01): KE 3888, UG 648, RW 182, TZ 1989, ZM 5537, ZW 718, MZ 161, BW 1557, NA 1470, AO 325, ZA 9674; BI 0 (Wikipedia: disappeared). Occurrences include captive or introduced records, so they support but do not prove native range. Excluded: MW 194 occurrences but not stated in the Wikipedia extent (open question).

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk: Wikipedia 'walk stiffly' during the rut. Gallop: judgement (the record's flee gait); no gallop speed is stated in Wikipedia. Leaping (jump up to 3 m) is described there but has no Hop mode in this record.

traits.nest_type.note: None: Wikipedia does not describe a nest; young are concealed in vegetation (judgement).

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia lead overall range 40-65 kg (sexes combined). Male and female description ranges are 53-76 and 40-53 kg.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Female minimum 40 kg and male maximum 76 kg from Wikipedia Description.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia lead overall shoulder range 70-92 cm.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia cites one analysis: about 45% monocots, 45% dicots and 10% fruit; mapped to graze, browse and fruit. The analysis is not identified; browse and graze are roughly equal and both are in the record. Dry-season browse is substantial per Wikipedia (grass use can reach 90% after first rains; browse predominates in dry season), so the single-food-tag program under-represents browse; see behavior note.

traits.social.note: Female herds 6-100 (Wikipedia, Ecology and behaviour); structure Group.

traits.defense.note: Flee: Wikipedia describes leaping over vegetation to escape predators.

habitat.note: Woodland and ecotone habitat, shade and water preference from Wikipedia. Shelter, water and resource weights are authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: No dormancy or migration is described.

seasonal.phases.note: No phase recorded. Wikipedia gives a three-week rut typically in May without region or population; seasonal is global in the schema, so a May phase would apply to every activity region including ZA. Not recorded until region-scoped evidence exists.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Males sexually mature by one year old (Wikipedia); the Juvenile duration is 365 days from that statement.

behavior.note: Shared program fsm-ground-forager-v1 takes one food_tag, so only graze is reachable. Wikipedia says impala 'browse as well as graze; either may predominate, depending upon the availability of resources', so browse (about 45% of diet by the cited analysis) is not reachable in the record. This is a known behavioural simplification that the shared program cannot express (two food tags or season-scoped food). Not defensible as complete; a species-local program is needed to represent browse. Rest window -90 to -6 degrees gives night rest as the program describes for a diurnal species.

look.note: judgement: stylised quadruped with a tan body, pale belly and dark legs; no proportion values sourced. Lyre horns and facial markings are not modelled.
